items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: But when we first went there, we were playing at Cadillac for a guy named Lee Larkins. That's the guy that sent for us, Lee Larkins.

ctx.x: Well, Reb was a fiery fellow, you know, see. So he told them that he wasn't going to do it, because there was no law against it, you see. There was no discrimination, and he wasn't going to stop it, you see. So the police said, all right, we're going to stop it, we're going to close you up. Well, he didn't believe it, I don't guess. He couldn't see the right people. So that next Sunday night, he come back down there. Three police come back there. Two colored police and a white blue. Detectives. So he called them…
And what kind of place was the cabaret? Cabaret. I clubbed his lap, just like Lee's.
